title: Role Design: Mandates That Partition
objective: After this lesson you will be able to write role cards (role/goal/backstory/tools) with non-overlapping testable mandates, detect overlap/gap failure pairs in review, and scope authority per role explicitly.
why: Agents with vague roles ('help customers', 'ensure quality') duplicate each other and diffuse responsibility — two agents email the customer, nobody owns the refund. Role cards partition accountability the way schemas partition data: each mandate owned by exactly one agent, each boundary testable. Role review happens before code because overlap found in prose is cheap and in production expensive.

blocks.text: A **role card** has four fields. **Role**: the job title it answers to ('Returns Triage Specialist'). **Goal**: the measurable outcome it owns ('every ticket routed within one step, zero unrouted'). **Backstory**: domain context shaping judgment (policies known, past patterns). **Tools/authority**: what it may touch — and implicitly, what it may not. The card predicts behavior: read it and state what the agent will and won't do.

blocks.caption: mustNot draws jurisdiction: what the role will never touch

blocks.text: Overlap and gaps: the failure pair

Two mandates covering one job → **overlap**: duplicated emails, double refunds, contradictory drafts. No mandate covering a job → **gap**: unowned failures ('nobody validates the amount'). Review pairwise: for each neighbor pair, state the shared boundary in one sentence ('triage routes; decider approves; neither drafts'). Unstatable boundaries are design debt.

blocks.caption: Shared-vocabulary audit flags candidate overlaps for human judgment

blocks.text: Tools follow authority: triage reads tickets; decider reads policy + facts; finance executes refunds (gated); support drafts only. Each tool grant answers 'what harm if misused?' — read-tools risk leakage (scope data), write-tools risk action (gate + log). The toolset audit (Ch.7) enforces this; role cards declare it.

blocks.title: Audit the roster
blocks.note: Run it: expect 2 flags. Triage × Quality is TRUE overlap (shared routing vocabulary — split or justify). Triage × Finance is a FALSE positive (shared words sit in mustNot: deliberate partition, dismiss with reason). Finance × Quality stays clean. Heuristics flag; humans decide — including dismissals.

items: Role cards: role/goal/backstory/tools + mustNot — jurisdiction by exclusion
Overlap (duplicated work) and gaps (unowned failures) are the failure pair — review pairwise with one-sentence boundaries
Tools follow authority; shared-vocabulary audits flag candidates, humans render verdicts

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the roster audit and report flagged pairs. (b) Rewrite the Quality role card so its mandate partitions cleanly from Triage (goal + mustNot), then re-run and confirm zero flags between them. (c) State the gap check: name one job in a returns flow no listed role owns, and assign it.
hints: Baseline: 2 flags — Triage × Quality (true overlap) plus Triage × Finance (mustNot false positive: shared words in an exclusion field mean deliberate partition — dismiss with reason).
Rewrite Quality as 'Review drafted replies against tone/length rules; never route tickets, never contact customers' — disjoint verbs, disjoint tools.
Gap candidates: amount validation, approval logging, quarantine review — assign each to an owner or create the role (gaps need names, not hopes).
exercise.why: Rewrite-to-green practices mandate surgery: same roster, partitioned verbs, proof by re-audit. Gap assignment completes the partition — every job owned, every owner exclusive.
exercise.code: // Partition checklist: pairwise one-sentence boundaries + gap sweep.

quiz.q: Two roles both 'ensure quality'. Failure mode?
options: Overlap: duplicated work + diffused responsibility — mandates must partition with testable boundaries
quiz.explain: Shared mandates duplicate effort and orphan accountability. One-sentence boundaries per pair, enforced by mustNot fields.

quiz.q: Nobody validates refund amounts. Failure mode?
options: Gap: unowned job — assign an owner or create the role; unowned work fails silently
quiz.explain: Gaps are overlap's twin: work nobody owns fails without an owner to page. Gap sweeps name every job's owner.

options: State jurisdiction by exclusion: what the role will never touch — reviewable authority boundaries
quiz.explain: Authority stated positively leaks ('may use tools' → which?). mustNot draws the fence explicitly: refunds, contact, execution — named and reviewable.

summary: Cards with jurisdiction (role/goal/backstory/tools/mustNot), pairwise overlap review, gap sweeps assigning every job. Partition accountability like schemas partition data.
next: Staffed with mandates — now the work orders: task specs with expected outputs that make handoffs hold. Next: delegation by contract.
